faq: Where do my leads come from?

Most teams use web forms, live chat, ads forms or email. Tell us the sources and we connect the ones your CRM supports. If a source cannot connect directly, we explain the simplest alternative before we build.
Can routing run by country or product?
Yes, on Standard and Premium. We build the rules from fields on the lead, such as country, product interest or deal size. Basic uses simple turn taking between your salespeople.
What if a salesperson is on holiday?
Standard adds a backup owner, and Premium also respects working hours. Leads then go to the next person in line, so no enquiry sits unanswered over a weekend or a day off.
Do you need access to my ad accounts?
Only if you want an ad lead form connected. Then you add us as a partner or user, never by sharing a password. Other sources, such as website forms, need only access to your CRM.

desc:
CRM lead routing rules setup sends every new lead to the right salesperson the moment it arrives. Ecom Swift LLC builds the rules in your CRM, tests them with sample leads and adds alerts and backup owners so nothing waits unseen.

## What is lead routing?

Lead routing is the set of rules that decides who owns a new lead. Instead of someone checking a shared inbox and handing leads out by hand, the CRM assigns each one automatically based on a condition you choose. That condition might be region, product, deal size, lead source or simple turn taking.

The goal is plain: the right person sees the right lead quickly, and every lead has exactly one owner.

## What happens when leads are assigned by hand

Manual assignment depends on whoever happens to be watching. A web enquiry arrives on Friday evening and sits until Monday. Two people reply to the same lead, or each assumes the other will. A request in French lands with a rep who only speaks English.

Speed matters here because a buyer who just filled in a form is comparing options right now. The first business to give a useful answer often shapes the whole conversation. Routing cannot make a lead buy, but it removes the avoidable delay between interest and a human reply.

## How routing improves fairness and response

Good rules do three jobs at once. They match leads to people who are best placed to help, such as a specialist for a product line or a local rep for a region. They spread the work evenly, so one person is not buried while another waits. And they make ownership visible, so a manager can see who holds what.

Alerts close the loop. The new owner gets a message at once, with the lead details, so the first reply is prompt and informed. Backup rules cover absence, which is where manual systems usually fail.

## What a solid routing setup includes

- Every lead source connected, such as web forms, ad forms, email enquiries or imports.
- Rules by region, product, deal size or tags, written in plain language.
- Turn taking between owners, with limits for working hours and days off.
- A backup owner for when someone is away or does not respond.
- A fallback owner for leads that match no rule, so none go unassigned.
- Notifications by email or message to the new owner.
- Duplicate checks, so a returning contact reaches the person who already knows them.
- A report of how many leads each owner received.
- A plain-language sheet explaining every rule to the team.

## How we do the work

We start by mapping your lead sources and asking how you would split them if you had unlimited time. Then we turn that into rules in your CRM, in an order that makes sense: specific conditions first, general ones after, and a fallback at the bottom.

Before anything goes live, we create sample leads for each case and check that each reaches the intended owner, including the awkward ones such as a lead with a missing country or two matching rules. The Basic package covers one source and a small group of owners. Standard adds more sources, rules by region or product and a backup owner. Premium adds rules by deal size and tags, turn taking within working hours and an owner report.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide who owns a lead when two rules both match.
- Name a fallback owner for unmatched leads.
- Tell the team how routing works before you switch it on.
- Review the owner report after a few weeks and adjust.
- Update the rules when someone joins, leaves or changes territory.

**Avoid:**
- Building twenty rules when three would do.
- Sending leads to people who are on leave with no backup.
- Splitting leads in a way that rewards the easiest territory.
- Rerouting existing deals without telling their owners.
- Forgetting to test a lead that arrives outside working hours.

## Who this service is for

It suits a growing team that has just hired its second or third salesperson and no longer wants the owner to hand out every enquiry. It suits a business with several offers or regions, where the right answer depends on who is best placed to reply. It also suits a company that buys leads from several sources and wants each one handled consistently.

## What we need from you

Tell us where your leads come from, who should receive which type and what should happen when someone is away. We need access to your CRM as an admin or similar user, and connections to your lead sources only where the setup requires it, such as a form or an inbox. We never ask for passwords, and we do not need access to your advertising accounts unless you want an ad form connected. Your CRM plan decides which assignment tools exist, and we check that before we begin.
